transcript:
[00:00] Morgan Ellis: hey everyone thanks for joining, im Morgan from Redwood, i'll run the agenda for today
[00:06] Dr. Hannah Lee: thanks Morgan, excited to dig in, we've got about 50 minutes, hope that's ok
[00:12] Morgan Ellis: perfect, we want to confirm success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, and integration path (SDK + openai-compat endpoints + function calling) and then next steps
[00:20] Priya Desai: hi all, quick intro, im Priya on the SE side, i'll own the bench and the POC run. real quick, can you remind us of your main latency/throughput needs?
[00:30] Marcus Yeo: sure, for our real-time assistant in the lab we need p95 under 200ms for short single-turn lookups, but for longer analysis flows 400ms is acceptable. target qps varies — baseline 30 qps, burst to 120 qps during batch ingest windows
[00:47] Priya Desai: ok got it, baseline 30, burst 120. are those evenly distributed or spikey?
[00:52] Marcus Yeo: pretty spikey; lots of small requests at start of day, then heavy backfills. also we use tool calling to hit an internal assay API and return structured JSON with fields for sample_id, result_code, confidence_score, and provenance_url
[01:08] Sofia Martinez: security question — all data is PHI-adjacent. we need audit logs, KMS integration, and proof of separation. do you offer customer-managed keys and retention controls?
[01:18] Morgan Ellis: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and we can surface audit logs; i'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs after this call. note: Private deployment adds setup time, we can also run a Dedicated instance with VPC peering for faster ramp
[01:33] Ethan Park: timeline wise, we'd like a pilot that completes in three weeks from kickoff if possible — proof of concept that demonstrates both performance and correct structured outputs
[01:42] Priya Desai: that's feasible — typical sprint: week 0 integrate SDK + openai-compat endpoints, week 1 run functional tests and tool-calling smoke tests, week 2 run throughput/latency benchmarks and then an acceptance eval. we can compress but need artifacts from you (traces, prompt sets)
[01:58] Dr. Hannah Lee: on structured output fidelity, we need at least 95% exact-field extraction on our golden set (50 test prompts). can you support structured schema enforcement or do we rely on post-parse?
02:10 Priya Desai: Redwood supports structured output via JSON schema and also function/tool calling; we can enforce response schema in the runtime and fail noisy outputs. small caveat: model variance can still produce malformed JSON occasionally, so we'll add post-parse validation in the client and an automatic reroll policy on the server side
[02:28] Marcus Yeo: curious about OpenAI-compat — can we reuse our current SDK wrapper? we already have internal code that expects the OpenAI Chat completions endpoint signature
02:38 Liam Cho: yes, Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible endpoints and an SDK that wraps both our native and openai-compat calls. swapping is minimal: same urs, same request body shape for chat/completions and function-calling. there are a few Redwood-specific parameters for routing and model variants but they're optional
[02:56] Marcus Yeo: nice. and function calling — we need the assistant to call our assay-run API which returns JSON. can Redwood's function-calling be proxied to internal APIs inside a VPC?
03:09 Priya Desai: yes, in Private or Dedicated with VPC peering we can route function calls to your internal endpoints. we also support a proxy connector to avoid opening direct inbound endpoints. we'll document the security posture for that
03:20] Sofia Martinez: does that proxy keep logs? we need auditability for every function invocation and the request payloads must be redacted at rest
03:29] Morgan Ellis: audit logs can include metadata and request hashes; payload retention and redaction policies are configurable. we'll include specifics in the security packet link I send after the call
03:38] Ethan Park: back to benchmarks — what metrics will you report?
03:42] Priya Desai: p50/p95/p99 latency per model/seq-length, tokens/sec, effective qps under continuous batching, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens estimate, and structured-output error rate on the golden prompts. we also capture KV-cache hit rates if you use long context sessions
03:59] Dr. Hannah Lee: what's your typical batch size/aggregation for low-latency workloads? we worry batching could push beyond our 200ms p95 target
04:08] Priya Desai: Redwood does continuous batching and dynamic batching configs; for low-latency we suggest small max_batch=4 and aggressive tail-latency SLO policing. in our bench we'll vary max_batch and target sequence length to find the sweet spot
04:23] Marcus Yeo: for model family, we're evaluating a mid-sized open model (7-13B) with 4-bit quant for cost, but we might need a larger model for reasoning flows. can you help pick quantization profiles?
04:36] Liam Cho: absolutely — Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and kernel profiles based on your prompt token distribution. for benching we'll test 7B quant and a 13B baseline for quality/latency tradeoffs
04:47] Dr. Hannah Lee: acceptance criteria recap: p95 < 200ms for short queries, structured field extraction >= 95% on golden set, throughput baseline 30 qps with sustained bursts to 120 qps, and security requirements met (KMS + audit logs)
05:05] Morgan Ellis: yep that's what we'll aim for. proposed pilot plan: 3 weeks, kickoff immediately after artifacts exchanged. Week 1 integrate SDK and endpoint mapping; Week 2 bench + tuning; Week 3 acceptance eval + report. if we hit targets we'll propose Dedicated or Private options with pricing and commit levels
05:24] Marcus Yeo: what about costs for benching? we prefer Redwood to run bench on your hosted infra vs us spinning up hardware — is that included or billable?
05:32] Priya Desai: initial bench for POC is complimentary within reason (couple of runs). extended long-running tests or dedicated reserved infra would be billable — we'll note that in the pricing sheet
05:43] Sofia Martinez: one more compliance question — do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for our team?
05:48] Morgan Ellis: yes, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC roles are supported. we'll include configuration notes
05:55] Dr. Hannah Lee: ok let's talk handoffs — who's owning infra provisioning and who runs the bench?
06:02] Priya Desai: Redwood SEs run the bench with your supplied traces and remote access to staging, we provide the scripts. Marcus/your team will validate outputs and confirm acceptance. Morgan will own commercial and security docs
[06:18] Ethan Park: can you also include a sample structured-output test harness so we can run evaluation locally?
06:26] Priya Desai: yes — we'll add a small pytest-based harness and a golden set runner in the example repo
06:32] Marcus Yeo: small nit — sometimes openai-compat params we rely on are named differently in other vendors, any breaking differences we should know about?
06:41] Liam Cho: largely compatible, but Redwood has routing fields like route_policy and model_hint. they're optional; if you don't include them calls map to your default project route. we can provide a compatibility shim in the SDK to make migration zero-change
06:56] Dr. Hannah Lee: good. final questions?
07:00] Sofia Martinez: please email the SOC2/ISO packet and a draft contract or SOW so security can triage next week
07:07] Morgan Ellis: will do. I'll also include the bench template and SDK quickstart link.
07:11] Ethan Park: thanks — excited to move forward
07:15] Morgan Ellis: great, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the kickoff for Dec 21 unless you want earlier
07:20] Dr. Hannah Lee: Dec 21 works. thanks everyone
[End of recording]
